```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
                      fig.align = "center")
```

Rogers, Blanchard & Mumby (2014, *Current Biology*) showed that the **structural
complexity** of coral reefs acts as a **size-structured prey refuge**: small and
mid-sized prey shelter in the reef matrix, which reshapes the community size
spectrum and the productivity available to fisheries. `dbpmr` implements this as
an opt-in per-size **availability** multiplier

$$a(w) = \max\!\big(\texttt{min\_A},\; 1 - \tfrac{\text{refuge}(w)}{\text{competitor}(w)}\big),$$

applied to **both** the predation mortality on, and predator intake of, prey of
body size $w$ (so sheltered prey are both eaten less and, as predators, hunt
less — matching the paper's `vulnerability()` function). With no refuge the
engine is bit-identical to standard `dbpmr`.

This vignette reproduces the paper's core qualitative result: **more complexity →
a bump in abundance at the sheltered sizes and a non-linear size spectrum.** The
paper's parameter `min.A` — the *minimum proportion of a size class that stays
vulnerable to predation* — is a natural **complexity axis**: `min_A = 1` is a
fully degraded reef (no refuge), small `min_A` is a highly complex reef.

## Setup

A minimal, unfished two-spectrum model, with a refuge over a band of mid-sized
prey (~1–30 g). We run it across a gradient of reef complexity by varying `min_A`.

```{r}
library(dbpmr)
LN10 <- log(10)

run_reef <- function(min_A) {
  wd <- tempfile("reef"); dir.create(wd); old <- setwd(wd); on.exit(setwd(old), add = TRUE)
  on.exit(Sys.unsetenv("REFUGE_MIN_A"), add = TRUE)
  run  <- Setup.Run("R", 1, 1, 0, TRUE, 1)
  grid <- Setup.Grid(run, tmax = 60, tstep = 1/48, toutstep = 1)
  pl <- Setup.Plankton(run, filename = "plankton")
  pe <- Setup.Pelagic(run, filename = "fish")
  be <- Setup.Benthic(run, filename = "benthos")
  de <- Setup.Detritus(run, filename = "detritus")

  if (min_A < 1) {                               # a refuge over the ~1-30 g prey band
    mass   <- seq(grid@mmin, grid@mmax, grid@mstep)
    log10m <- mass / LN10
    refuge <- ifelse(log10m >= 0 & log10m <= 1.5, 1e20, 0)  # strong shelter -> a clamps to min_A on the band
    Setup.Refuge(pe, run, grid, refuge, min_A = min_A)
  }
  invisible(capture.output(SizeSpectrum(run, grid, pl, pe, be, de)))
  f <- Read.In("R", "fish")
  data.frame(log10m = f@mrange / LN10, u = as.numeric(f@finaluvals[1, -(1:3)]))
}
```

## Complexity gradient

`min_A = 1` is the degraded baseline (no refuge); `0.5` and `0.2` are increasingly
complex reefs.

```{r}
degraded <- run_reef(1.0)    # no refuge
medium   <- run_reef(0.5)
complex  <- run_reef(0.2)    # strong refuge
band <- degraded$log10m >= 0 & degraded$log10m <= 1.5
```

```{r fig.height = 4.2, fig.width = 9}
sel <- degraded$log10m > -4 & degraded$log10m < 5 & degraded$u > 0
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.2, 3, 1))
# (left) the three spectra
plot(degraded$log10m[sel], log10(pmax(degraded$u[sel], 1e-30)), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#9ecae1",
     xlab = expression(log[10]~"body mass (g)"), ylab = expression(log[10]~"abundance density"),
     main = "Size spectra")
lines(medium$log10m[sel],  log10(pmax(medium$u[sel],  1e-30)), lwd = 2, col = "#4292c6")
lines(complex$log10m[sel], log10(pmax(complex$u[sel], 1e-30)), lwd = 2, col = "#084594")
rect(0, par("usr")[3], 1.5, par("usr")[4], col = rgb(0, 0.4, 0, 0.06), border = NA)
legend("topright", c("degraded (min_A=1)", "medium (0.5)", "complex (0.2)"),
       col = c("#9ecae1", "#4292c6", "#084594"), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
# (right) effect relative to the degraded baseline -> the refuge bump is obvious
rel <- function(d) log10(pmax(d$u[sel], 1e-30)) - log10(pmax(degraded$u[sel], 1e-30))
plot(degraded$log10m[sel], rel(complex), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#084594",
     xlab = expression(log[10]~"body mass (g)"), ylab = expression(Delta~log[10]~"abundance vs degraded"),
     main = "Complexity effect (refuge bump)")
lines(degraded$log10m[sel], rel(medium), lwd = 2, col = "#4292c6")
abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
rect(0, par("usr")[3], 1.5, par("usr")[4], col = rgb(0, 0.4, 0, 0.06), border = NA)
text(0.75, par("usr")[4] * 0.85, "sheltered band", cex = 0.8, col = "darkgreen")
legend("topright", c("complex (0.2)", "medium (0.5)"), col = c("#084594", "#4292c6"), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

Increasing complexity (smaller `min_A`) lifts abundance **in the sheltered band**
and bends the spectrum away from a straight line — the paper's non-linear,
refuge-driven size spectrum.

```{r}
data.frame(
  reef       = c("degraded", "medium", "complex"),
  min_A      = c(1.0, 0.5, 0.2),
  band_vs_degraded = round(c(
    mean(degraded$u[band]) / mean(degraded$u[band]),
    mean(medium$u[band])   / mean(degraded$u[band]),
    mean(complex$u[band])  / mean(degraded$u[band])), 2)
)
```

The sheltered-size abundance rises monotonically with reef complexity — i.e. a
**loss of complexity reduces** the abundance those sizes can sustain, the
direction of the Rogers et al. (2014) result (there, quantified as a >3× loss of
fisheries productivity under full complexity loss).

## Notes

* **Reduced form.** This is a two-spectrum (`U` + `V` + detritus) model; the full
  2014 reef model also carries a herbivore spectrum and an algae pool (the
  competitor pool there is `U + H`). A control re-run of the Rogers R model
  confirmed that even a two-spectrum refuge reproduces the bump, so this captures
  the core mechanism as an honest reduced form.
* **Off by default.** With no `Setup.Refuge()` call the mechanism is inactive and
  the engine is bit-identical to standard `dbpmr`.

### Reference

Rogers A, Blanchard JL, Mumby PJ (2014) Vulnerability of coral reef fisheries to
a loss of structural complexity. *Current Biology* 24(9): 1000–1005.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2014.03.026>
